rejected.why: Factor of Subdivision - a different quantity built ON the margin-line framework, and the card assumes the datum rather than defining it.

adjudications.ask: Whether sea water or fresh water may be pumped overboard directly from a cargo hold.
adjudications.evidence: A permission question with a real answer: hold water is not bilge water from a machinery space, its treatment turns on what the hold last carried and on the cargo residue and washing-water rules, and 'just pump it out' is the trap. The bank covers Annex V through its certificates, record books and amendments, and covers hold flooding through damage control, but no card asks whether the discharge itself is permitted or on what condition.

rejected.why: Latest amendments to MARPOL Annex V - regulatory currency, not a discharge-permission decision.
Statutory certificates under Annex VI - wrong annex and a certificates question.
Annex V record books and the onboard procedure - what is recorded, not whether this discharge is allowed.
Comprehensive statutory certificate list under SOLAS and MARPOL.
Greenhouse gases under Annex VI - matched only on the word Annex.

adjudications.ask: A vessel carrying weapons anchored beyond 24 nautical miles - which convention applies and who takes action.
adjudications.evidence: Two limbs, neither on the bank. The zone limb turns on 24 nautical miles being the outer edge of the contiguous zone, so a ship anchored beyond it is outside the coastal State's contiguous-zone enforcement powers and the question becomes one of flag State jurisdiction and of the SUA Convention regime rather than of UNCLOS zones alone. The bank teaches the zones and it teaches war-risk and armed-guard practice, but nothing joins arms aboard a ship to who may act against her, which is the whole of the ask.

rejected.why: Sovereign rights versus jurisdiction as UNCLOS concepts - definitional, and never applied to a ship carrying arms.
UNCLOS in general plus rights denied in a war-risk area; the contiguous zone limit and enforcement against an armed ship are not in it.
